Key Research Thinking Patterns: Digital Polarimetric Phased Array Radar Design: Development of a fully digital polarimetric phased array radar, Horus, which uses a unique digital-at-every-element architecture to enable rapid and adaptive scanning, and has the potential to provide accurate and reliable weather observations.

Hybrid Optimization for Beam Synthesis: A hybrid optimization method for synthesizing beam patterns using phase-only and constrained-loss magnitude/phase weights to exploit beamforming capabilities of the Horus radar, accounting for practical antenna performance and synthesizing different types of transmit beam patterns.

Phase-Only Beamforming for Polarimetric Weather Radars: A novel technique for generating multiple simultaneous transmit beams using phase-only beamforming weights, leveraging Bézier surfaces to parametrize the phase excitation across the array, reducing the number of variables in the search space and achieving high-quality polarimetric measurements during severe weather events.

Space-Time Adaptive Processing: Utilization of runtime re-configurable broadened-beam digital subarray strategy to rapidly scan a large region of space, resulting in a volumetric dataset with many planned and unplanned targets and features, and demonstrating strong weather returns and target detection capabilities.
Summary Description: Mark Yeary is a researcher specializing in the development of advanced radar systems, particularly in the areas of digital polarimetric phased array radar, beamforming, and space-time adaptive processing. His work focuses on creating high-resolution weather observations and improving the accuracy of weather forecasting, severe weather warning systems, and air traffic control. Utilizing cutting-edge techniques such as phase-only beamforming, hybrid optimization, and Bézier surfaces, Yeary's research aims to overcome the challenges of combining polarimetric and phased array technologies, ultimately leading to more accurate and reliable weather observations and improved decision-making in various application domains.
